title: VATS-targetable grenades always show 0% hit chance on PC
status_note: Runtime-verified for the temporary in-session hook; FNVBug001Fix v4 installed, pending restart verification that the xNVSE-loaded module owns the two patches and one queued grenade shot executes.
platform: PC; reported working on Xbox 360 and PS3
summary: Vanilla creates a VATS entry for an airborne grenade with body-part index -1. Its highlight/body-part lookup fails, so the live update path skips FUN_007F1290 and leaves entry+0x28 at exactly 0.0; the grenade shows 0% and cannot be preselected. The v4 hook accepts grenade targets at that failed lookup and lets the existing vanilla chance resolver run.
hypothesis: CONFIRMED: at 0x007F4544, FUN_00800A00 rejects the grenade's body-part index -1; the branch at 0x007F454E then skips the live chance call at 0x007F45C7. FUN_00646F70 is not globally dead: FUN_007F1290 calls it at 0x007F158E. The omission is target-type-specific.
measured: Clean vanilla runtime: selected grenade entry+0x28 remained 0.0 and repeated clicks never reached the downstream click/chance probe. With the exact two-site Stewie-equivalent hook active, one selected grenade stored 0.098696 (displayed 9%) and exposed Accept. Repeated tests with three airborne dynamites produced distinct, reasonable percentages; sampled internal values included 0.086298, 0.098696, 0.153444, 0.186391, 0.295660, 0.316435, 0.394239, 0.423925 and 0.482302.
root_cause: The grenade-target entry exists and the vanilla resolver exists, but the live update path rejects the grenade before calling it. The missing integration is the body-part/highlight fallback for a target whose body-part index is -1.
fix_direction: Match lStewieAl's bTargetProjectilesInVATS implementation: detour the call at 0x007F4544 so a failed normal lookup succeeds when currentTarget's vtable+0x224 predicate identifies a grenade, and redirect FUN_00800A00's fallback float operand at 0x00800A7D from 0x01012054 to a plugin-owned 0.2f. Do not poll entry memory or bypass the zero-chance gate.

sources.label: Runtime causality proof

sources.label: Falsified hypothesis
sources.detail: FUN_00646F50 (+0x124 max-range) is weapon range, not projectile range - irrelevant to this bug

falsification_trail.result: FALSIFIED by runtime patch — returning 500.0 changed nothing
falsification_trail.lesson: FUN_00646F50 is the equipped weapon's max-range accessor, not the projectile range

falsification_trail.hypothesis: FUN_00646F70 (VATS target resolver with grenade branch + 'destructible/grenade target chance' debug string) computes the displayed chance
falsification_trail.result: RETRACTED after live-path recovery — FUN_007F1290 calls it at 0x007F158E. The earlier callgraph export was incomplete, and forcing its return changed nothing only because the grenade path never reached FUN_007F1290.
falsification_trail.lesson: Distinguish a target-specific skipped caller from globally dead code; capture call-site execution before promoting a zero-xref result.

falsification_trail.hypothesis: The zero-chance gate at 0x007EEA46 controls queueing
falsification_trail.result: PATCH APPLIED (test ah,0x44 -> test ah,0x00) but targeting still blocked
falsification_trail.lesson: The displayed 0% itself is what blocks targeting — the fix must change the computed chance value, not the gate

atlas_findings.pc_alignment: PC FUN_007EC810 (contains the zero-chance gate) aligns to vtable slot 11 = Xbox VATSMenu::DoIdle
atlas_findings.implication: The patched gate lives in DoIdle (per-frame). The click/queue path is DoClick (PC 0x7EECB0) which contains no direct chance-field access — the block happens deeper in the attack-execution chain

dead_code_finding: SUPERSEDED: FUN_007F52C0 creates live grenade target entries, and FUN_007F1290 calls FUN_00646F70 at 0x007F158E. Runtime capture showed grenade targets alone miss that call because FUN_00800A00 rejects body-part index -1 at 0x007F4544/0x007F454E.

shipped_fix.mechanism: v4: PDB-matched two-site engine hook. The call at 0x007F4544 is detoured to accept grenade targets after a failed normal body-part lookup, and the fallback multiplier pointer at 0x00800A7D is redirected to 0.2f. Vanilla then continues to FUN_007F1290/FUN_00646F70.
shipped_fix.verified: Temporary in-process copy of the exact hook produced a 9% selectable grenade with Accept enabled, followed by three airborne dynamites with different reasonable percentages. The permanent x86 DLL builds warning-clean and is installed for the next xNVSE launch.
shipped_fix.limitation: Permanent next-launch module/patch ownership and a queued-shot execution still require post-restart verification. The prior v3 flat/fabricated-distance DLL is retained only as FNVBug001Fix.dll.disabled.

v3_design: SUPERSEDED: the poller used unproven VATSTargetData coordinate fields and a fabricated 50000-unit falloff, causing flat 95% behavior. It is not the fix.

superseded_thrown_weapon_analysis.source: FUN_00646F70 thrown-weapon branch (0x006471A1-0x00647330), decompiled instruction-exact. This branch describes the player using a thrown weapon; it is not the airborne-grenade target branch for a currently equipped gun.
superseded_thrown_weapon_analysis.formula:
maxRange    = weapon->maxRange                        // FUN_00646F50 reads this+0x124
mult        = fVATSGrenadeRangeMult                   // 2.0
if (maxRange * mult <= targetDistance)                 // 0x006471C1 gate
    return 0.0;                                        // "Target out of thrown weapon range"

modMaxRange = maxRange * mult
rangeGap    = modMaxRange - fVATSGrenadeRangeMin      // falloff measured from the 128-unit ideal arc
distDelta   = |targetDistance - fVATSGrenadeRangeMin| // distance FROM the sweet spot
rangeOdds   = 1.0 - distDelta / rangeGap              // 0..1, =1 at the sweet spot

skillArg    = target ? FUN_00446390(...) : 0
skill1      = FUN_00646880(attacker, skillArg)        // per-attacker skill term
if (skill1 <= 0)
    armCondition = 1.0
else
    armCondition = 1.0 - fCrippledArm1HSpreadPenalty  // crippled arm: 0.8

FUN_008D85E0();
skill2      = FUN_0066EF50(actor)                     // __thiscall actor skill query
t           = fVATSGrenadeSkillFactor * skill2 / 100  // 0.4 * skill2/100
skillTerm   = ((1.0 - fVATSSkillFactor) + t) * armCondition

chance      = (rangeOdds + skillTerm) * fVATSGrenadeChanceMult * 100.0   // 1.0 * 100
// for destructible/grenade targets: chance *= 100 again, clamp: if (0 < chance < 1) chance = 1

skill_functions.FUN_0066EF50: __thiscall SkillCalc2(actor) - vtable+0xC query then FUN_0066F190 transform

superseded_thrown_weapon_analysis.bug_classification: Historical misattribution retained for auditability. The formula is valid for thrown-weapon use, but the BUG-001 target path is repaired earlier at the VATS body-part/highlight lookup.

fix_verified: Runtime-verified for the temporary exact hook: 0%/unselectable became computed 9%/selectable, and three airborne dynamites produced different reasonable chances. This validates preselection, clickability, and non-flat computation without a gate bypass.
remaining: Verify the installed v4 DLL after a fresh xNVSE launch and execute one queued grenade shot; do not describe the installed artifact as startup-verified until then.

title: iSneakLevelBonus can invert the intended sneak modifier
summary: When the player is above an actor's level, the level modifier can become negative and make sneaking harder. GECKWiki points directly at engine address 0x642ED0. YUP has documented the behavior and ultimately reverted its own gamesetting workaround because the underlying calculation remains bugged for some actors.
hypothesis: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED by static analysis (2026-09-04): 0x642ED0 is the sneak detection-value accumulator. It adds (arg24 - arg23) * iSneakLevelBonus at 0x642F10-0x642F1C with a signed, UNCLAMPED integer multiply - the only level term in the function without a max(0, ...) clamp (the neighboring iSneakStartBonus term is clamped via max helper 0x647B70 at 0x642F3D). When the player out-levels the actor, this term goes negative, matching GECKWiki's 'multiplication results in a negative modifier'. Settings confirmed via ctor thunks: iSneakLevelBonus=obj 0x11CD13C (default 5), iSneakStartBonus=0x11CD8C0 (50), iSneakStartBonusLevelPen=0x11CD4C0 (10), fSneakBaseValue=0x11CD7E4 (-25.0), fSneakAmbushTargetMod=0x11CDBF8, fSneakAmbushNonTargetMod=0x11CD1E0, fSneakPerceptionSkillMin=0x11CDF04, fSneakPerceptionSkillMax=0x11CDD9C. SECOND-DEFECT ANGLE (community): YUP found the setting 'always miscalculates the bonus for certain actors' even when nonzero - creature actor-level getters (Ghost People reach level 50) may return unexpected values; test creature vs NPC targets separately in the runtime A/B.
re_findings: Sole caller: call site 0x8A152D inside the detection updater FUN_008a0d10. Accumulator seeded from arg2, perception-skill scale and ambush/lighting factor tail confirmed instruction-exact. Ghidra decompile (research/re/decompiled/FUN_00642ed0_00642ed0.c) gives the decisive line: total -= ((max(0, iSneakStartBonus - L2*pen) + (L2 - L1)*iSneakLevelBonus + arg2 - arg25) * flag) * floatSetting. arg23/arg24 are both actor levels fetched with the identical +0xA4 -> vtable+0x28 (movzx ax) getter in the caller. arg4 sneak skill resolved via actor-variable getter 0x5E58F0 (AV bound 0x4A, player singleton 0x11DEA3C). Full working notes in research/re/engine-glossary.md section 3.1.
root_cause: The level-difference term (param_24 - param_23) * iSneakLevelBonus is raw signed integer arithmetic with no clamp, while the sibling start-bonus term is deliberately clamped with the engine's own max(0,.) helper 0x647B70. When the two actor levels are ordered so the difference is negative, the sneak 'bonus' becomes a penalty (harder to sneak), matching the GECKWiki report and the 'multiplication results in a negative modifier' note at 0x642ED0.
fix_direction: Clamp the level-difference term with the same max(0,.) helper used by the start-bonus sibling (behavior-preserving when the bonus should only ever add). Operand-swap is the alternative if runtime A/B shows the intended polarity is actor-level minus player-level rather than 'only positive'. Design decision pending the player-vs-actor direction test.
next: Runtime A/B on the GOG 1.4.0.525 + xNVSE: two saves, player above vs below an actor's level, measure detection threshold shift; confirm sign direction; then implement the clamp patch (NVSE plugin, following the FNVBug001Fix two-site pattern) and verify the bonus can no longer invert.
research: No engine fix. YUP v11.2 zeroed iSneakLevelBonus, v12.0 reverted it ('still bugged and always miscalculates the bonus for certain actors') - implying a second defect beyond the sign issue, possibly the actor-level getter for creatures (Ghost People reach level 50; mods 86023/78398/60519 target exactly those). fallout.wiki Detection Formula documents the intended math: (Sneak + iSneakLevelBonus*(TargetLevel-DetectorLevel) + max(iSneakStartBonus - pen*TargetLevel,0) - ArmorPenalty); engine GMST name is literally misspelled 'iSneakStartBonusLevelPenatly' in docs.

title: RemoveAllItems / RemoveAllTypedItems skip normal unequip lifecycle
summary: GECKWiki reports that mass-removal commands do not execute OnUnequip blocks and can leave effects behind. Older modder reports also describe partially removed equipped armor and corrupted inventory state.
hypothesis: CONFIRMED by static analysis: the bulk-removal path bypasses the equipment teardown. RemoveItem (0x5B4E90) checks IsEquipped (0x575400) and runs the unequip teardown (0x8248E0 / 0x41AB70 family) before invoking the vtable+0x17C remove per item. RemoveAllTypedItems (0x5B55A0) instead calls the shared inventory-remove primitive FUN_004CE340 + list rebuild FUN_00952C30 with no IsEquipped check and no unequip call. RemoveAllItems' console handler (0x5B1570) is a parser/re-emitter dispatching through the command table function pointer at record+0x1C.
root_cause: Bulk removal goes straight to InventoryChanges-style removal (0x4CE340) and never enters the equip/unequip lifecycle, so OnUnequip blocks never fire and persistent magic effects applied at equip time are never torn down. The single-item path proves the lifecycle functions exist and are wired (0x575400 IsEquipped -> 0x8248E0 -> vtable+0x17C); the bulk path simply omits the loop that routes equipped entries through them.
re_findings: Console command anchors (GOG clean image): RemoveAllItems name 0x1040B74/struct 0x1192418/exec 0x5B5690; RemoveAllTypedItems 0x103E114/0x1196478/0x5B55A0; RemoveItem 0x1041268/0x11915E0/0x5B4E90; UnequipItem 0x1040584/0x1192E68/0x5D0300. Command struct layout: name @+0x0 (slot), exec @name_slot+0x18, shared post-mod callback 0x5B1BA0 @+0x1C. DECOMPILED (2026-09-04): RemoveAllItems exec FUN_005b5690 calls FUN_004ce380(refr, item, 0, silent, 0, flag, 0xffffffff /*count=-1 remove-all*/, 0) + FUN_00952c30(refr) rebuild - NO IsEquipped/unequip anywhere. RemoveItem exec FUN_005b4e90 conversely performs per-item: 0x575400 IsEquipped -> 0x8248E0 teardown -> vtable+0x17C. The 6.8KB primitive 0x4CE380 itself contains no unequip machinery in its 48 callees. Analysis record in glossary section 3.3.
fix_direction: Route equipped entries through the same IsEquipped(0x575400)->teardown(0x8248E0)->vtable+0x17C sequence the RemoveItem handler performs, applied at the two bulk exec call sites (0x5B5690 / 0x5B55A0). Do NOT patch the shared primitive 0x4CE380 - it has three callers including engine path 0x54B5B0 and lacks unequip internally by design. Shared with FNV-BUG-028 and FNV-BUG-029 (same mechanism, different observable symptom).
next: Runtime repro on clean GOG vanilla: scripted armor with an observable OnUnequip block + enchantment effect, equip, RemoveAllItems, assert no block fire + effect remains. Then prototype the NVSE-plugin fix mirroring the RemoveItem teardown sequence and re-run repro.
research: No public engine fix - our static root cause is the deepest analysis available. ShowOff's RemoveAllItemsShowOff (v1.15+) is a reimplementation with its own documented bugs (exception formlists ignored, flags unreliable); JohnnyGuitar fixed only the cosmetic backpack-remains variant. xNVSE source calibration: Cmd_EquipItem_Execute=0x5D0060, Cmd_UnequipItem_Execute=0x5D0300 - the latter independently confirms our static exec finding for UnequipItem. Modder workaround: JIP UnequipItemAlt/getAllItemRefs loop before removal.

title: NPC armor enchantments stack again every time the NPC loads
summary: GECKWiki reports that enchantments on NPC-worn armor can be reapplied on each load and stack indefinitely.
re_findings: 2026-09-04: equipped-walker FUN_008249d0's enchant gate resolved - FUN_005f36f0 is a PLAIN FIELD GETTER returning [EnchantmentItem+0x34]; the walker updates visuals only when that field is 0. The stacking defect is upstream: whoever ADDS EnchantmentItem entries on actor load (equip-restore path) does not dedupe. Next: identify +0x34 semantics in xNVSE GameMagicForms.h EnchantmentItem layout and trace the actor-load equip-restore add path for the missing has-equivalent check.
hypothesis: Actor load/equipment restoration reapplies the armor effect without checking for an existing equivalent active effect or without restoring the effect as recovered state.
next: Runtime verify: NPC with enchanted armor, cycle cell unload/reload N times, assert effect magnitude/value stacks N-deep (GetActorValueC or effect listing); then prototype the dedupe patch as an NVSE hook on the activation branch.
research: No public fix anywhere (zero YUP changelog hits for enchant/stack across all 13 versions; nothing in UPNVSE+/Stewie/JIP/ShowOff). Wiki's own speculation matches our plan: missing 'has effect' check or recovery-flag handling on actor load.
root_cause: ROOT CAUSE (static, 2026-09-04): the equip-change handler FUN_008c48d0 activates worn-item enchantments after checks that are purely type-based: form-type gate (vtable+0x18 == 6 armor family), the enchant cast, and EnchantmentItem+0x34 == 2 (an enchantment slot/type test via getter 0x5F36F0) - plus a FUN_00639B40 match check that only suppresses in narrow conditions (form 0x29 / param_4 flag). There is NO 'does the actor already have this effect active' dedupe anywhere in the path. NPC load restores equipment by re-running this equip path, so each load adds another active copy of the armor enchantment - matching the wiki's 'no has-effect check' speculation. The SAVELOAD 'Enchantable item ... created base objects list' diagnostic confirms load-time re-processing.
fix_direction: Add an active-effect dedupe (or recovery-flag respect) in the enchant-activation branch of FUN_008c48d0: before applying, query the actor's active effects for an existing instance from the same EnchantmentItem (the query helper family used by the walker gate 0x5F36F0/+0x34 state is the natural hook point).

title: Actor templates in leveled lists are selected disproportionately often
platform: New Vegas; reported working in Fallout 3
summary: GECKWiki reports that if an actor template is itself in a leveled list, it is almost always chosen. The Fallout 3 comparison makes this another useful engine-differential target.
re_findings: 2026-09-04 pass 10: PlaceLeveledActorAtMe exec FUN_005d9810 decompiled - resolves args, dispatches by form type 0x2A (TESLevCharacter, 0x1C8-byte ctx via FUN_008D1D30) vs 0x2B (TESLevCreature, 0x1C0-byte ctx); the spawn/selection logic is downstream of the dispatch. Selection-defect trace continues from the 0x2A/0x2B branches; 0x7701E0 is the level-vs-player consumer.
hypothesis: The New Vegas leveled-actor selection path treats template entries differently during eligibility filtering or random weighting.
next: Build a controlled LVLC/LVLN test with equal-weight template and non-template candidates, gather selection frequencies, then trace the leveled actor picker and compare against Fallout 3/Xbox evidence where available.
research: No engine fix; YUP/TTW patch individual lists and the standing guidance is 'do not place actor templates in leveled lists in NV'. Stewie's adjacent note that code at 0x7701E0 'looks fine' (Living Anatomy DT case) places 0x7701E0 inside the leveled-actor iteration region - a direct secondary anchor. TESLeveledList layout from xNVSE: datas +0x4, chanceNone +0xC, flags +0xD.

title: AI packages fail to process correctly while the player is away
platform: New Vegas; reported working in Fallout 3
summary: Sleep, find, patrol and eat packages may fail to advance unless the player enters the cell, crosses a load door, or fast-travels, even when low-level processing should apply.
re_findings: Swap dispatcher FUN_008d0660 + all four migration handlers decompiled: High 0x8D9FA0 (~20 fields + 2 lists), MiddleHigh 0x914C60 (177 lines, incl. dialogue cleanup FUN_00496080), MiddleLow 0x92CA70 (9 lines - the defect), Low 0x907510 (32 lines). Process classes RTTI-confirmed via xNVSE symbol table (High 0x118A6D4, MiddleHigh 0x118C64C, MiddleLow 0x11A3668, Low 0x11A364C).
hypothesis: New Vegas selects the wrong process level or skips package ticks for unloaded actors under some package categories.
next: Runtime verify: patrol/sleep actor observed off-cell before/after a re-bucket trigger, package timestamps; then enumerate the missing field set for FUN_0092ca70 vs siblings and prototype the extended migration.
research: No fix for the core bug. The process hierarchy is fully named in xNVSE GameProcess.h: BaseProcess::processLevel at +0x28 (High/MiddleHigh/MiddleLow/Low), ActorProcessManager buckets middleHighActors/lowActors0C/lowActors18/highActors, MobileObject+0x87 holds the inverse of NoLowLevelProcessing, baseProcess at +0x68. Community theory matches ours: freshly loaded actors left in the wrong bucket until a cell transition forces re-bucketing.
root_cause: ROOT CAUSE (static, 2026-09-04): the process-swap dispatcher FUN_008d0660 routes each level pair to a dedicated migration handler. High->High (FUN_008d9fa0) migrates ~20 state fields plus two lists; MiddleHigh->MiddleHigh (FUN_00914c60, 177 lines) migrates extensive package/dialogue state; but MiddleLow->MiddleLow (FUN_0092ca70) is NINE LINES - it copies one dword at +0xB4 and migrates a single list at +0xB8, dropping everything else. Middle-low is exactly the level where off-screen actors run sleep/find/patatrol/eat packages; when an actor is re-bucketed (spawn, cell attach, load) into middle-low, its package/timer state is not carried over, so packages stall until a cell transition forces higher-level processing. Fix direction: extend FUN_0092ca70 to migrate the same state family the sibling handlers carry (field-level list to be enumerated against FUN_00914c60/FUN_008d9fa0).

title: Combat / CAUTION state can remain stuck after threats are gone
summary: Combat or caution may persist after moving to a cell with no alerted actors or after enemies die; GECKWiki marks this as only partially fixed by JohnnyGuitar.
re_findings: 2026-09-04 anchors: '[CAUTION]' HUD/status string @0x105B3F4 referenced at 0xF6F0C3 (caution-state display/aggregation); sSneakCaution @0x105B3E4. Community-confirmed engine addresses (JG NVSE source): GetPlayerInCombat=0x953C50, bFixFleeing patch site 0x8F5FE2, combat-music routine 0x992D90 (call site 0x82FC0B), named Actor::TrespassAlarm/StealAlarm. State holders: HighProcess::combatTarget +0x404, detectedActors +0x25C / detectingActors +0x260, fAwarePlayerTimer +0x34C. The latch defect is in whatever clears combatTarget/SetAlert(false) - trace from GetPlayerInCombat's readers.
hypothesis: One or more detection/combat participants remain registered or a global/player combat-state aggregate is not invalidated on unload/death transitions.
next: Runtime verify: aggro an enemy, kill it while hidden (no combat-end bark), observe CAUTION/DANGER persist; console GetPlayerInCombat before/after. Then prototype the aggregate-clear hook.
research: 'Partially fixed by JG' but the specific sub-fix is undocumented. JG internals pin absolute addresses: engine GetPlayerInCombat=0x953C50, bFixFleeing patch site 0x8F5FE2, combat-music routine 0x992D90 (call site 0x82FC0B), plus named Actor::TrespassAlarm/StealAlarm. Struct state: HighProcess::combatTarget +0x404, detectedActors +0x25C / detectingActors +0x260, fAwarePlayerTimer +0x34C. Community theory: combat state latches when the last alerted actor dies or unloads before a combat-end event fires.
root_cause: ROOT CAUSE (static, 2026-09-04): the player's combat aggregate is the byte at PlayerCharacter+0xDF0 (GetPlayerInCombat 0x953C50 returns it; +0xDF1 is the secondary flag it can write out). The engine's combat-target clear routine FUN_008c5ef0 (called from FUN_0091ebb0's null-target branch) tears down the PER-ACTOR target structure: nulls the target, conditionally clears PlayerCharacter+0x208 (last-hit target), resets timers - but it NEVER clears +0xDF0/+0xDF1. Those aggregate bytes are maintained by the detection/combat-event feed (HighProcess detectedActors +0x25C family) and have no invalidation path when the last alerted actor DIES or UNLOADS without a combat-end event; the state then latches until some transition re-runs the full teardown (reload). Exactly the wiki report and the JG 'partially fixed' remit (JG hooked consumers like GetPlayerInCombat 0x953C50 / combat music 0x992D90, not the latch itself).
fix_direction: Add a clear of PlayerCharacter+0xDF0/+0xDF1 when the last combat participant is removed: hook actor-death/unload removal into a check over the detecting/detected lists and reset the aggregate when empty - or patch FUN_008c5ef0 to also clear the aggregate when it clears the player's +0x208 entry.

title: GameMode scripts on crafted items do not run until drop + pickup
summary: GECKWiki reports that crafted scripted items do not begin running GameMode blocks until the item is dropped and picked up.
re_findings: 2026-09-04 anchors: OnAdd console/script event exec = 0x5CA200 (command struct name-slot 0x118E368 - adjacent to SayToDone's struct, same command block); ShowRecipeMenu command name @0x103E074 for the crafting output path. JIP's fixed OnAdd-on-crafted bug (wiki Bugs Fixed list) and this GameMode variant share the crafted-item insertion path - diff the recipe-menu output insertion against normal AddItem insertion starting from these anchors.
hypothesis: Crafting creates the inventory entry without the initialization/event path that attaches or activates the object script instance.
next: Craft a minimal scripted item with an incrementing variable, compare AddItem vs crafting vs drop/pickup, then trace recipe-menu output insertion against normal inventory insertion.
research: The OnAdd variant was fixed in JIP LN NVSE but only partially ('armors and non disposable weapons'); the GameMode variant remains unfixed anywhere. Crafted items are runtime-created forms with modIndex 0xFF (xNVSE Hooks_CreatedObject.cpp); xNVSE names engine function 0x471870 in the created-object ref-name path. Theory: the script instance is not attached the normal way until a full drop+pick-up add cycle.

title: Ballistic projectiles ignore defined water impact decals
summary: Non-hitscan projectiles using full ballistic flight modeling reportedly fail to use water impact decals even when the impact data set defines them.
re_findings: 2026-09-04 pass-15 refinement: the three ballistic callers are TRAJECTORY PLANNERS (FUN_009a7670 = two-pass aim/flight sampling calling FUN_009a6e90; consumes only hit position for targeting) - they apply no impact data. The decal application on ballistic impact therefore lives in the projectile-hit dispatcher (the same family JIP's ProjectileImpact event hooks), not in the planners. Next hop: obtain JIP's projectile-impact hook address from JIP-LN-NVSE source (internal/hooks.h) and decompile the vanilla dispatcher; the water-material skip is in its impact-data consumption vs the hitscan branch.
hypothesis: The ballistic collision path bypasses or misclassifies the water-material impact branch used by hitscan projectiles.
next: Create matched hitscan and ballistic weapons using the same impact data, reproduce at controlled water surfaces, then compare impact-dispatch call paths.
research: No public fix. JIP source documents the structures fully: BGSImpactData (model, effectOrientation, soundLevel, textureSet, decalInfo sub-struct) and BGSImpactDataSet.impactDatas[materialID <= 11] (12 material slots, water is one) plus runtime GetProjectileRefImpactMaterial - the material lookup and decal data exist and are runtime-mutable; only the ballistic flight path fails to consume them. JIP's hookable ProjectileImpact event gives the diff point vs the hitscan path.

title: Moveable objects can warp to worldspace coordinates (0,0)
summary: Mostly frag mines are reported to warp to worldspace (0,0) when cells two grids away are loaded for the first time.
re_findings: 2026-09-04 anchors: Havok warp machinery - ini keys 'fCharControllerWarpDistSqr:HAVOK' @0x10C4AF4 and 'bFindContactPointsOnAdd:HAVOK' @0x10C42EB (the latter is the OnAdd contact-point path implicated when cells first load), fHavokTauRatio gamesetting @0x10561F0, ExtraHavok RTTI TD @0x1183B50. The (0,0) warp is an uninitialized world transform during first-load boundary registration - these are the candidate code owners.
hypothesis: A cell-transition or Havok handoff uses an uninitialized/default world transform during first-load boundary registration.
next: Build a reproducible exterior grid setup with logged reference positions, find the first-load transition that changes the transform, then inspect cell/Havok registration code.
research: No public fix (nothing in YUP/VNV/Stewie INI). The 'two grids' trigger matches the uGridsToLoad streaming ring - grep the exe for that INI key to reach the first-load attach path; the (0,0) target suggests a zero-initialized float2 world-transform write in cell attach. Mine state machine anchors: projFlags & 0x200 (armed), base flags (0x426)==0x26.

title: Looping weapon/object sounds survive reload or disable transitions
summary: GECKWiki lists several related lifecycle failures: looping weapon audio can replay after death-load, and disabled objects can continue emitting looping sounds.
re_findings: 2026-09-04 anchor: RTTI '.?AVExtraActivateLoopSound@@' TypeDescriptor @0x11851A8 (name @0x11851B0) -> COL 0x1104F70 -> vtable 0x1015F18. The activate-loop-sound extra-data class owns looping sound lifecycle on references; its teardown-on-disable/save-load path is where the stuck loop bug lives.
hypothesis: Looping sound handles are not consistently stopped when their owning reference is disabled, unloaded, or reconstructed from a save.
next: Split into weapon-reload and disabled-object repro cases, capture sound-handle lifecycle, and identify the teardown path omitted by the failing transition.
research: Death-load ghost loop: no public fix (sibling spin-weapon loop fixed by Stewie's bSpinWeaponsSoundFix at engine level). Audio internals from JIP GameSound.h: BSGameSound kFlag_Loop=0x10, kState_IsLooping=0x20000, SetIsLooping vtable+0x14, kRequestType_StopAllSoundsWithFlags=0x2A. Theory: loop handle owned by audio manager survives death-load because the load path issues no stop for orphaned loops; second load's teardown reaches it.

title: SayToDone fails when the speaker is outside the player's cell
summary: SayToDone reportedly does not fire for an actor outside the player's current cell regardless of persistence/quest status. Related Say/SayTo package-result calls can hang when the player is elsewhere.
re_findings: 2026-09-04 ROOT-CAUSE CANDIDATE: SayTo exec FUN_005c9100 decompiled. The speech-queue branch (FUN_00934250 path) is gated at line ~87 on actor vtable+0x22C returning true and audio-owner 0x8D8520 being non-null; when the speaker is outside the player's cell this gate fails and the SayTo request is silently dropped - the completion event (SayToDone condition 0x5CA1C0/0x5CA950) is never armed. OnAdd exec FUN_005ca200 identified as a thin poll of the same shared event-predicate family. Remaining: identify vtable+0x22C (expected = in-player-cell / 3D-loaded predicate) and confirm which caller arms the completion flag.
hypothesis: Dialogue completion notification is tied to the high-process actor/audio update path rather than persistent script/event state.
next: Runtime verify: two-cell SayTo repro with persistent speaker (SayToDone block var before/after); identify vtable+0x22C's name via the Xbox vtable atlas; then prototype.
research: No fix for the cross-cell gate (NVSE saytodone event is the workaround). Engine anchors from JG/xNVSE source: ScriptEventList::MarkEvent=0x5AC750 (hook return 0x5AC756), Say completion code at 0x5791C1 (SayToTopicInfo), kEvent_SayToDone=0x40000, blocktype opcode 07. Community theory converges with our static finding: off-cell actors are not high-processed so the say-completion callback never runs - matches the vtable+0x22C gate we located in SayTo's exec.
root_cause: ROOT CAUSE (static, 2026-09-04): the Say-completion marker FUN_00579160 exists and works - it resolves the say-context (FUN_0042EDE0), checks the context's active flag (+0x18), and marks kEvent_SayToDone (0x40000) on the speaker's ScriptEventList via MarkEvent (0x5AC750). But it has ZERO direct callers: it is registered as a callback in a function table at 0x102F69C. That table is consumed by the dialogue/audio completion dispatcher, which only ticks for speakers on the high-process path - SayTo's own exec (FUN_005c9100) refuses to queue speech unless the actor passes vtable+0x22C and the audio owner (0x8D8520) exists. An off-cell speaker therefore never gets the completion callback, the 0x40000 flag is never marked, and the SayToDone block/condition never fires regardless of persistence - exactly the wiki report. Package-result Say hangs follow the same missing completion.
fix_direction: Queue the completion marking for off-cell speakers: either run FUN_00579160's marking from a low-process-safe path (timer/audio-owner independent), or relax the vtable+0x22C gate in SayTo's exec so speech is queued for persistent off-cell actors with the completion callback armed. NVSE-plugin hook style per BUG-001.

title: AI dialogue package Once a Day flag is inconsistent
platform: New Vegas; reported working in Fallout 3
summary: GECKWiki remaining-bug seed; reproduction matrix still needed.
re_findings: 2026-09-04 anchor: RTTI type descriptor '.?AVExtraSayTopicInfoOnceADay@@' @0x118521C - the extra-data class implementing say-once-a-day semantics. Next: recover the complete-object-locator/vtable from this TypeDescriptor to get the class methods (the once-per-day check + its reset condition), then compare against the FO3 behavior the wiki says works.
research: No public fix. kPackageFlag_OncePerDay=0x400; run-once state lives in the per-actor package stack (BaseProcess run-once virtuals, MiddleHighProcess::interruptPackage +0xE4, PackageInfo at BaseProcess+0x4). Theory consistent with 'works in FO3': the once-per-day timestamp is stored per package-stack entry and resets on interrupt/re-push or is not persisted across save/load.
root_cause: ROOT CAUSE (static, 2026-09-04): ExtraSayTopicInfoOnceADay (extra type 0x73, ctors 0x437440/0x437510) has exactly ONE construction call site in the entire binary: 0x429300, which lies inside ExtraDataList::LoadGame (FUN_00428150, 17KB, 144 callees - the save-load extra-data switch). The once-per-day tracking extra is therefore ONLY instantiated when restored from a save; the in-session say path never creates it. Consequently the once-a-day gate has no state to read on a fresh session (or reads state restored from an earlier day), so the Once a Day package flag behaves inconsistently depending on save/load history - matching the wiki's 'works inconsistently (works in Fallout 3)' report.
fix_direction: Create/refresh the OnceADay extra at say time: hook the topic-info say path (or the package executor testing kPackageFlag_OncePerDay=0x400) to construct extra 0x73 with the current game day if absent, mirroring what the save-load path restores. NVSE-plugin style.
next: Runtime verify: fresh session (no prior save-load of the actor), trigger a Once a Day package twice in one day - expect both fire; after a save+load, expect the gate holds. Confirms the absent-in-session mechanism.

title: Aggro Radius Behavior can suppress packages indefinitely
summary: Actors with Aggro Radius Behavior may stop executing packages near the player even when non-hostile after enough game time has elapsed.
re_findings: 2026-09-04 pass 19: HighProcess vtable recovered (COL 0x111E5C4 -> vtable 0x1087864). vt+0x20C = FUN_008d83e0, a trivial forwarder to the pointer-getter - i.e. the 'aggro violated' query reads a stored actor pointer on the process. The set/clear pair decompiled: FUN_0091ebb0 (set target; null branch calls flush vt+0x214/vt+0x12C) -> FUN_008c6080 (stores target+timestamp+form into the per-actor combat struct at this+0..0x10) and FUN_008c5ef0 (clear). The violation/latch persistence is in WHO calls the set with the player and never re-calls clear when the radius is exited - the set path stores timestamps (this+0x10) suggesting a timed decay inside the process tick; the 'constant aggro' is that decay never firing for non-hostile actors. Next hop: xref callers of 0x91EBB0/0x8C6080 with the aggro flag (TESAIForm+0x13) to find the insert site and its missing decay/remove.
research: No engine fix for the constant-aggro behavior; Stewie's adjacent fix only prevents weapon-holster suppression when the radius is breached. TESAIForm::aggroRadiusBehavior at +0x13 and aggroRadius at +0x14 (few readers - fast to pinpoint). Theory: the player-aware latch (fAwarePlayerTimer HighProcess+0x34C family) is never reset when the player leaves the radius.

title: Stonewall does not reduce creature attack damage
summary: Creature attacks are reportedly classified as neither melee nor unarmed for Stonewall's damage reduction test.
re_findings: 2026-09-04 pass-17: CheckConditionFilters = FUN_005ea060 - validates each filter form (vtable+0xE4 actor check, else vtable+0xF0 weapon-form fallback, else 'Bad Filter form' diagnostic) then evaluates each condition via FUN_00680C60. Stonewall's melee/unarmed classification is therefore a DATA-DRIVEN condition on the perk's PRKE filter (evaluated by 0x680C60's condition-function dispatch), not hard-coded in the apply handlers. Static trail complete: entry-point name table 0x1045E00+, apply-handler table 0x11973C0, registry 0x1197400, validator 0x5E5B80, filter checker 0x5EA060, condition evaluator 0x680C60. The wrong-actor-weapon theory (checks player's weapon instead of attacker's) is now precisely testable: read Stonewall's PRKE filter + condition from the ESM, map its condition function to the engine handler, and check which actor's equipped weapon it queries.

title: StartCombatResponse can select the wrong speaker
summary: The response path reportedly fails to check other actors and can make the initiating actor speak a line it should not.
research: No public fix. StartCombatResponse is a dialogue-function-table entry (FO3 DIAL table 0x80d81, used in vanilla DLC barks). Theory: response-selection never validates speaker candidacy of nearby actors. Anchors: 'StartCombatResponse' string in exe + the fCombatDialogue* GMST readers (shared processor with BUG-027).
root_cause: ROOT CAUSE (static, 2026-09-04): the combat-response processor FUN_009839b0 contains a full other-actor selection pass - iterates the actor list (FUN_004FB070/GetCount), skips self and the player, gates candidates through process vt+0x30C/0x22C/0x20C checks, picks the NEAREST by distance (FUN_00527A40, lines ~197-225) and says the chosen topic through that actor (vt+0x280, line ~268). BUT the whole pass is guarded by local_21 (init ''), which earlier code CLEARS when the original actor has pending state (process vt+0x214 nonzero path, lines ~136-146) or meets the 0x1A/0x1C form-type conditions. With local_21==0 the selection is skipped, the nearest-other search never runs, and the fallback (line ~227 'if none found use self' plus the line ~262 branch vt+0x2A4) makes the ORIGINAL actor say the line. The wiki's 'does not check other actors' is precisely this skipped-branch: the pending-state flag disables the check, so lines meant as responses from others are spoken by the initiator.
fix_direction: Stop clearing local_21 on the vt+0x214 pending-state condition (or re-run the other-actor pass regardless and only fall back to self when the list is empty). Patch site: the flag-clear branches at ~0x983Bxx-0x983Cxx in FUN_009839b0; NVSE hook style.
next: Runtime verify: pair of actors with combat-response topics; place the responder mid-package (pending state) and confirm the initiator speaks the line; then with the patch, confirm the responder speaks.

title: Dialogue hit sounds have no cooldown
summary: Creatures hit by automatic weapons can spam dialogue sounds continuously because the line/sound path lacks a cooldown.
re_findings: 2026-09-04 CORRECTED: GetHit console exec FUN_005d5630 is a DEBUG command (prints 'GetHitLocation >> %%0.2f' via 0x703C00); the runtime 'GetHit' string push at 0x5D566C is inside this same debug function, NOT the hit->dialogue trigger. Retracted that anchor. The real BUG-027 site is the damage->combat-dialogue event dispatcher - the same machinery JIP LN NVSE patched for 'Player/NPC hit dialogue does not work' (wiki Bugs Fixed list). Next anchor: locate JIP's hit-dialogue patch sites in JIP-LN-NVSE source (internal/hooks.h) and map back to the vanilla dispatcher; the missing cooldown is in the topic-selection call there.
research: JIP v55.45 'Fixed dialogue combat reactions/comments, all of which were completely broken' is the adjacent public fix. DECISIVE EVIDENCE: JIP settings_enum.h enumerates the full combat-dialogue cooldown GMST family WITH addresses - Attack/Flee/FireExplosive/AvoidThreat/Detection pairs (e.g. fCombatDialogueAttackMinElapsedTime @0x11CFB20, Max @0x11CE4C8; fCombatDetectionDialogueMinElapsedTime @0x11CF0B0) - and TELLINGLY NO 'Hit' elapsed-time GMST exists in the family. The cooldown selector's switch has no hit arm: every qualifying hit re-triggers a Say. Also bDisableCombatDialogue [Combat] @0x11F1764 as a clean anchor.
root_cause: ROOT CAUSE (static, 2026-09-04): the combat-dialogue processor FUN_009839b0 (contains the sole runtime reader 0x983D04 of the cooldown settings) implements per-type Min/Max elapsed-time cooldowns ONLY for bark types 0/1 (attack), 3, 4, and 5 in both its topic-selection switch and its cooldown switch - case 2 (the hit-reaction type) is absent from both. No fCombatDialogue*Hit* GMST exists anywhere in the binary (confirmed by string scan), so hit reactions are structurally excluded from the per-type cooldown system; the only remaining gate is a single global 1500ms throttle (_DAT_011f170c check at 0x9839xx, 0x5DC), far too coarse for automatic-weapon hit rates. Every qualifying hit therefore re-triggers a Say.
fix_direction: Add the missing case-2 arm to both switches in FUN_009839b0 with a Hit Min/Max GMST pair (new settings or reuse the detection pair), or hook the processor to apply the detection-family cooldown to hit reactions.
next: Runtime verify: creature target + automatic weapon, count barks per magazine before/after; then prototype the case-2 cooldown patch.
